newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end mostly up on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end mostly up on short-covering.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly up on Thursday on short-covering from retail investors after falls over the past few days, traders said.
The most actively traded September 1997 contract ended at an intraday high of 3,150 yuan ($378) per tonne, rising 10 yuan. It opened at 3,150 yuan and hit a low of 3,130 yuan per tonne.
November was unchanged at 3,160, the January 1998 contract rose one to 3,132 and March fell 11 to 3,140 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume rose to 25,500 tonnes from 20,400 tonnes.
Soybean opened mostly up and moved in a narrow range for most of the session, traders said.
